settings.heading: How to get started
settings.content: Use it on a flat, non-slip surface with the knee mat. Kneel, rest your forearms on the pads and hold the handle. Brace your core and roll forward a short distance, then guide the return. Start with a few slow reps and build up over time.

settings.heading: Safety
settings.content: Stop if you feel pain, especially in your lower back or shoulders. If you have a back, joint or other health condition, are pregnant or recovering from surgery, check with a doctor before using. Not for children.

settings.heading: Questions?
settings.sub: Know your equipment. Build your routine.

settings.a: A four-wheel ab roller with padded forearm rests, a spring-assisted return, an adjustable handle and a built-in phone rest. A knee mat is included.

settings.q: How does the spring-assisted return work?
settings.a: Steel springs inside the wheel housing help pull the roller back as you return to the start. You still control the speed and how far you roll.
Yes. Start from your knees with a short range of motion and a few slow reps, then build up gradually. Stop if you feel pain.
Rollouts mainly train your core, and your shoulders, arms and back work to stabilise you.

settings.q: Does it need an app or batteries?
settings.a: No. It is fully mechanical. The phone rest simply holds your own phone if you want a timer or video in view.

settings.q: Will it give me visible abs?
settings.a: No piece of equipment can promise that. Visible results depend on your overall routine, nutrition, sleep and starting point.

settings.q: Who should check with a doctor first?
settings.a: Anyone with back, shoulder, wrist or joint problems, people who are pregnant or recovering from surgery, or anyone unsure whether core exercise is right for them.

settings.text: Begin with a supported kneeling rollout, keep a comfortable range, and make core training part of your everyday routine.
